note: Four N-terminal/conformational anti-tau antibodies cut tau in FTD-mutant (P301L/P301S) mice and all failed in amyloid-positive early-to-moderate AD despite engaging N-terminal tau; a human AD-seed assay had called them weak in 2018.
label: Alzheimer's (anti-tau mAb)

engagement.note: Lilly's MC1 and PHF1, dosed peripherally, cut tau pathology in JNPL3 and P301S mice; no human readout existed yet.
engagement.short: Anti-tau antibodies engage tau in mutant mice
engagement.quote: We show that peripheral administration of two antibodies against pathological Tau forms significantly reduces biochemical Tau pathology in the JNPL3 mouse model.
engagement.judgement: Opens the FTD-mutant tau-transgenic track at the first sponsor-relevant passive-immunization study (MC1 is zagotenemab's murine parent; Fleisher 2024 cites these JNPL3/P301S data as its preclinical basis). Yanamandra 2013 (HJ8.5, tilavonemab's parent, infused into P301S mice) is the same system making the same prediction, so it shares this track rather than opening another.

engagement.note: Systemic tau rose after dosing in tau-transgenic mice, monkeys and phase 1 humans; AD participants rose more than healthy controls.
engagement.short: Plasma tau rose in mice and humans
engagement.quote: Semorinemab also showed clear evidence of target engagement in vivo, with increases in systemic tau concentrations observed in tau transgenic mice, nonhuman primates, and humans.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level only: Science Translational Medicine paywall, no PMC copy. The abstract says murine versions of semorinemab were used for mouse efficacy; which antibody gave the mouse PD readout is not stated. Phase 1 NCT02820896 has no posted results.
engagement.judgement: One paper puts mouse, monkey and phase 1 human PD side by side, so comparison_stated is true; subjects mixed (healthy controls and mild-to-moderate AD). Readout is antibody-bound tau accumulating in plasma, a measure of the antibody on its target, scored direct.
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of systemic total-tau change after dosing

engagement.note: Gosuranemab cut unbound N-terminal tau in patient CSF at every dose, as it had in mouse interstitial fluid.
engagement.short: CSF unbound N-terminal tau fell at all doses
engagement.quote: At week 76, all doses caused significant (P < 0.0001) reductions in the cerebrospinal fluid levels of unbound N-terminal tau compared to placebo.
engagement.reason: N-terminal tau engaged as mice predicted
engagement.judgement: Strengthens, not a status change; the same paper states the mouse side ('In preclinical studies, gosuranemab robustly removed N-terminal tau from brain interstitial fluid'). Engagement is of N-terminal tau only: Florian 2023 reports tilavonemab CSF free tau -38% at 2000 mg, and Fleisher 2024 says of zagotenemab 'There was no direct biomarker evidence of central tau target engagement' despite dose-related plasma tau rises, so engagement of aggregated, seeding-competent tau stays unshown for the conformational member; that gap is scored under efficacy.
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of unbound N-terminal tau change (mouse ISF vs patient CSF)

engagement.model: AD-patient-derived cortical-neuron eTau in human neurons and two human-tau transgenic mouse lines
engagement.note: IPN002's lineage antibodies neutralized eTau purified from AD-patient neuron media, lowering Abeta in human neurons and two human-tau mouse lines; no human Abeta readout yet.
engagement.short: eTau neutralization lowers Abeta in model
engagement.quote: We found that neutralizing eTau reduces Aβ levels in vitro in primary human cortical neurons where exogenously adding eTau increases Aβ levels.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Elsevier paywall, no PMC copy): the abstract names neither the two human-tau transgenic lines nor the antibody clone; Courade 2018 identifies antibody A (WO2014028777A2, IPN002) as the antibody 'developed to bind an N-terminal fragment of Tau hypothesized to potentiate beta amyloid accumulation [3]', citing this paper.
engagement.judgement: Separate track under the run's identity rule: patient-derived eTau in human neurons with an Abeta readout is a different system from the P301 mice and makes a different prediction (Abeta falls when eTau is neutralized). The in-vivo arm's mouse lines are unverified, so the track is named by its distinctive patient-derived component.

engagement.model: AD-patient-derived cortical-neuron eTau in human neurons and two human-tau transgenic mouse lines
engagement.note: Gosuranemab cut CSF unbound N-terminal tau at every dose, yet week-76 CSF Abeta42 moved no more than placebo (-1.90% high dose vs -3.81%).
engagement.short: CSF Abeta42 unchanged despite tau capture
engagement.quote: Levels of the amyloid-β isoform Aβ42 in the CSF were also measured, and the changes from baseline at week 76 were small and comparable between groups
engagement.confidence_note: Paired comparison: Shulman 2023 (PMC10724064, full text read) reports CSF Abeta42 but cites neither Bright 2015 nor the eTau-to-Abeta hypothesis; the Abeta42 readout is not among the outcomes posted on the registry (2022-11-08), so the comparison dates to the paper. The model side is read at abstract level.
engagement.reason: Abeta did not fall as eTau model predicted
engagement.judgement: The model's stated prediction was that neutralizing eTau lowers Abeta. In TANGO the antibody removed unbound N-terminal tau from CSF at all doses (P < 0.0001) but Abeta42 did not change against placebo (-8.99 pg/ml, -1.90%, high dose; -17.38 pg/ml, -3.81%, placebo), so the downstream readout the model used did not move: contra, readout downstream. product_in_model false: Bright used the IPN002 lineage, not the humanized product. The N-terminal-tau readout itself is the existing mouse track's and is not re-scored here.
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of Abeta change: model predicted a fall, CSF Abeta42 change indistinguishable from placebo

engagement.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
engagement.note: The product itself depleted unbound N-terminal tau from PSP and AD patient CSF ex vivo and removed seeding-competent tau from AD brain homogenate.
engagement.short: Ex-vivo CSF and AD-lysate depletion assays
engagement.quote: Immunodepletion of pathological human brain homogenates and transgenic mouse interstitial fluid (ISF) with gosuranemab resulted in reduced tau aggregation in tau biosensor cells.
engagement.judgement: Opens the sponsor's own ex-vivo track at first publication; the humanized product, not a murine parent, was used (product_in_model true).

engagement.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
engagement.note: Ex-vivo depletion of unbound N-terminal tau in PSP/AD patient CSF matched the >90% CSF suppression seen in dosed cohorts.
engagement.short: Ex-vivo CSF depletion matched clinical CSF engagement
engagement.quote: These results are consistent with the >90% target engagement observed in the CSF of some clinical trial dosing cohorts and support the evaluation of gosuranemab as a potential treatment for AD.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The paper postdates the clinical CSF data it cites (Qureshi 2018 healthy volunteers 67-97%; Boxer 2019 PSP 90-96%); whether the ex-vivo CSF experiment was run before those readouts is not stated, so a checker may rule this a retrodiction.
engagement.judgement: Stated comparison in the model paper itself: ex-vivo depletion of unbound N-terminal tau in patient CSF against the dosed cohorts' CSF suppression. Readout direct (free target). subjects mixed: healthy volunteers (phase 1) and PSP patients; AD patients' CSF engagement followed in TANGO (Shulman 2023, all doses P < 0.0001). Scored same rather than retro because the ex-vivo unbound-tau assay is the bench form of the clinical PD assay and plausibly preceded it; flagged low confidence.
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction and extent of unbound N-terminal tau depletion (ex-vivo patient CSF vs dosed-cohort CSF, >90%)

dose.note: Mice were dosed peripherally with MC1 and PHF1; no human exposure target existed to compare.
dose.short: Mouse dosing; no human target yet
dose.quote: We show that peripheral administration of two antibodies against pathological Tau forms significantly reduces biochemical Tau pathology in the JNPL3 mouse model.
dose.judgement: Opens the dose strip at the track's first use; the mouse regimen is a proxy for an exposure target the sponsors later derived by modeling.

dose.model: P301L tau-transgenic mice + exposure modeling of extracellular-tau binding
dose.note: Exposure modeling put sufficient extracellular-tau binding at 4500 mg; plasma tau saturated above 4500 mg, yet CDR-SB did not move at 1500-8100 mg.
dose.short: Target exposure reached; no efficacy at any dose
dose.quote: More participants were allocated to the placebo and 4500-mg semorinemab arms to increase the power of comparisons between these groups, as preliminary exposure modeling suggested sufficient binding of extracellular tau species at the 4500-mg dose.
dose.confidence_note: The exposure model itself is unpublished; its preclinical PK/PD basis (Ayalon 2021) was read at abstract level.
dose.judgement: v3 dose table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': the binding target set from the preclinical PK/PD was met (dose-dependent plasma tau rise saturating above 4500 mg; CSF:serum 0.3%, consistent with phase 1) and a dose nearly twice it (8100 mg) also failed, so the dose cell takes the efficacy failure once, as contra derived_from efficacy. Teng: 'it remains unclear what central nervous system levels of monoclonal anti-tau antibodies might be needed to meaningfully interrupt the spread of pathological tau'. No member hit a toxicity ceiling, so decision 16 does not apply.

dose.note: All gosuranemab doses cut CSF unbound N-terminal tau (P<0.0001), the mouse ISF target, and none changed CDR-SB at week 78.
dose.short: ISF target met in CSF; CDR-SB unchanged
dose.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control
dose.reason: Target reached at every dose; no benefit
dose.judgement: Same v3 row for a second member (strengthens). Florian 2023 adds tilavonemab: CSF free tau -38% at 2000 mg, 'the doses assessed were sufficient to engage CSF tau', and 'no improvement in the primary or key secondary end points with increasing tilavonemab exposures'. Fleisher 2024 says zagotenemab's phase 2 doses rested on nonclinical and phase 1 PK/PD yet found no direct biomarker evidence of central target engagement, so for that member the target may never have been shown reached; it does not change a contra track.

efficacy.note: MC1 and PHF1 cut tau pathology in JNPL3 mice and delayed motor decline in P301S mice; HJ8.5 did the same in P301S mice (Yanamandra 2013).
efficacy.short: Anti-tau antibodies cut tau in mutant mice
efficacy.quote: We show that peripheral administration of two antibodies against pathological Tau forms significantly reduces biochemical Tau pathology in the JNPL3 mouse model.
efficacy.judgement: First passive anti-tau antibody efficacy in tau-transgenic mice by a sponsor (Lilly) whose antibody (MC1 -> LY3303560/zagotenemab) reached phase 2; Fleisher 2024: 'In preclinical mouse models, on treatment with MC-1 (a murine equivalent), tau pathology was reduced in genetic variant mice (JNPL3 mice) and blocked in models of tau seeding (P301S mice).'

efficacy.model: Human AD-brain PHF-tau seeding assay (HEK293 P301S-tau biosensor cells)
efficacy.note: Antibodies recreated from the gosuranemab and tilavonemab patents were inactive (A) or partial at high concentration only (B) against AD-brain tau seeds.
efficacy.short: N-terminal antibodies fail to block AD seeds
efficacy.quote: Generally, Tau antibodies binding the N- (antibodies A and B) or C-termini (antibody E) do not efficiently neutralize Tau seeds from Alzheimer's disease.
efficacy.confidence_note: Courade names antibodies A and B only by patent (WO 2014/028777A2; US 2015/0183855 A1) and epitope (N-terminus, cut off at residues 24 and 30; A 'developed to bind an N-terminal fragment of Tau hypothesized to potentiate beta amyloid accumulation'); the mapping to gosuranemab (IPN002, aa 15-24) and tilavonemab (HJ8.5, aa 25-30) is my inference from those epitopes and patents, not stated in the paper.
efficacy.judgement: A separate track under the run's identity rule: a different system (patient-derived AD PHF seeds in a cell assay, no transgenic mouse) making the opposite prediction to the FTD-mutant mice, published before any of the four phase 2 trials read out (first results posting 2022-03-16). Its own data: 'While antibody A was essentially inactive in this assay, antibody B did show activity against AD Tau, but only at high concentrations.'

efficacy.model: P301L tau-transgenic mice (4R tau, murine surrogate of semorinemab)
efficacy.note: Murine semorinemab cut tau in P301L mice; semorinemab moved neither CDR-SB nor tau-PET in 422 amyloid-positive prodromal-to-mild AD patients.
efficacy.short: Mouse tau reduction not replicated in Tauriel
efficacy.quote: It remains uncertain why the preclinical efficacy of the murine surrogate of semorinemab for reducing tau accumulation was not replicated in the Tauriel study.
efficacy.judgement: Teng's own explanations: the N-terminal epitope may be absent from the tau species that spread in early AD, and 'the P301L transgenic mouse model ... overexpresses 4R tau (as opposed the mixed 3R/4R tau seen in AD)'. Lauriet (Monteiro 2023, mild-to-moderate AD, same antibody) later met one co-primary (ADAS-Cog11, -42.2%) but not ADCS-ADL and 'this study was negative'; under the one-contra-beats-one-same rule, with no tier 1-4 evidence that the Tauriel signal attenuated, the track stays contra and Lauriet is logged in the 2023 entry's patient_trials.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of tau-pathology and clinical change

patient_trials.quote: semorinemab did not slow clinical AD progression compared with placebo throughout the 73-week study period but did demonstrate an acceptable and well-tolerated safety profile.

efficacy.model: Human AD-brain PHF-tau seeding assay (HEK293 P301S-tau biosensor cells)
efficacy.note: Antibody A, gosuranemab's sequence, was essentially inactive against AD seeds; gosuranemab then failed TANGO, as did the other three N-terminal/conformational members.
efficacy.short: Assay called N-terminal antibodies weak; all failed
efficacy.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired comparison: no source puts Courade's assay beside the trial results, though Teng 2022 and Shulman 2023 both cite it and reach the same explanation (N-terminal epitopes miss the seeding-competent, microtubule-binding-region tau that is scarce in CSF). The antibody-to-product mapping is inferred from epitopes and cited patents.
efficacy.reason: Assay predicted the failure before trials
efficacy.judgement: Year is the registry posting of TANGO results (2022-11-08), the earliest date both sides of this paired comparison were public; the earlier member postings (Tauriel 2022-03-16, tilavonemab 2022-08-26, zagotenemab 2022-08-30, Lauriet 2022-10-03) are in patient_trials. Scored neg rather than same because the assay's own number for a member's V-region (antibody A, inactive) fell below the assay's selection bar and that member failed (decision 13). Semorinemab (aa 6-23) and zagotenemab (MC1 conformational epitope) were not among Courade's reference antibodies and are covered only by the class-level N-terminus statement. Lauriet's ADAS-Cog11 hit is a partial exception to the assay's prediction but the trial missed its co-primary. Florian 2023 (tilavonemab) draws the same lesson: 'anti-tau antibodies directed against the N-terminus may be less effective than those that target the mid-domain region.' product_in_model false: antibodies A and B carry the clinical V-regions in a mouse IgG1 backbone, not the products.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction: no seed neutralization predicted, no clinical effect observed
efficacy.effect_size: antibody A (gosuranemab/IPN002 V-region): essentially inactive up to 300 nM against AD-PHF seeds; antibody B (tilavonemab/HJ8.5 V-region): 74% neutralization, high concentrations only
efficacy.class_threshold: full neutralization of AD-PHF seeding, the assay's selection bar (antibody D: IC50 2.9 nM, 98% inhibition at 300 nM)

patient_trials.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control
semorinemab did not slow clinical AD progression compared with placebo throughout the 73-week study period
Tilavonemab was generally well tolerated but did not demonstrate efficacy in treating patients with early Alzheimer's disease.
In participants with early symptomatic AD, zagotenemab failed to achieve significant slowing of clinical disease progression compared with placebo.
Based on the results of the prespecified coprimary endpoints, this study was negative.

efficacy.note: All four members cut tau in P301L/P301S mice and all failed in early AD; the authors call the models unsuitable for extracellular-tau drugs.
efficacy.short: Four mouse successes, four clinical failures
efficacy.quote: However, similar to gosuranemab, these agents have failed to demonstrate a clear clinical benefit in patients with early AD, calling into question the predictive value of these mouse studies for clinical efficacy.
efficacy.reason: Mice cut tau; patients did not
efficacy.judgement: Class-wide stated comparison, kept as a strengthening entry: 'The tau transgenic mouse models used in these preclinical studies typically express the human 4R tau isoform with the frontotemporal-dementia-associated P301L or P301S substitution' and 'these models are unsuitable for testing therapeutics aimed at intercepting extracellular tau'. TANGO's primary objective was safety with CDR-SB the pre-specified efficacy gate (endpoint_role poc_gate); the other members' trials had clinical primaries (CDR-SB, iADRS, ADAS-Cog11/ADCS-ADL co-primaries). product_in_model null: gosuranemab's own ISF data are cited, the other three used murine surrogates.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of tau-pathology and clinical change

patient_trials.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control
Tilavonemab was generally well tolerated but did not demonstrate efficacy in treating patients with early Alzheimer's disease.
In participants with early symptomatic AD, zagotenemab failed to achieve significant slowing of clinical disease progression compared with placebo.
Based on the results of the prespecified coprimary endpoints, this study was negative.

efficacy.model: P301S mouse-brain-lysate tau seeding biosensor assay (HEK293 FRET cells)
efficacy.note: HJ8.5, tilavonemab's parent, was selected because it blocked P301S-lysate seeding at 0.25 ug/ml, the most potent of the panel; no patient result existed.
efficacy.short: HJ8.5 picked for blocking mouse seeds
efficacy.quote: Using a cell-based biosensor assay, we screened anti-tau monoclonal antibodies for their ability to block seeding activity present in P301S brain lysates.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3924573 author manuscript via NCBI efetch).
efficacy.judgement: Separate track under the run's identity rule: the mouse-seed counterpart of Courade's AD-seed assay, a different seed source that made the opposite prediction for the same V-region (full blockade here; 'partial activity against AD-PHF Tau' only at the highest doses as antibody B in Courade 2018). Its in-vivo arm (HJ8.5 infused into P301S mice) stays on the tau-tg-mice-p301 track. Own data: 'The HJ8.5 antibody blocked seeding activity at concentrations as low as 0.25 μg/ml compared to controls.'

efficacy.model: P301S mouse-brain-lysate tau seeding biosensor assay (HEK293 FRET cells)
efficacy.note: Tilavonemab, humanized HJ8.5, missed CDR-SB at 300-2000 mg in 453 early AD patients; the mouse-seed assay had ranked HJ8.5 the most potent seed blocker.
efficacy.short: Mouse-seed blocker failed in early AD
efficacy.quote: Tilavonemab was generally well tolerated but did not demonstrate efficacy in treating patients with early Alzheimer's disease.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired comparison (Florian 2023 does not cite Yanamandra 2013 as a prediction); patient side read at abstract level; registry results posting 2022-08-26 is the earliest both sides were public.
efficacy.reason: Blocked mouse seeds; no clinical effect
efficacy.judgement: Courade 2018 had already found the same V-region (antibody B) 'demonstrated partial activity against AD-PHF Tau, neutralizing seeding activity by 74%' and only 'abruptly and only at the highest doses tested', so the two seed sources disagreed before the trial and the AD seeds were right. Primary endpoint CDR-SB (registry confirmed). Tilavonemab's 2019 PSP failure (Hoglinger 2021) is another indication and is not scored here.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of seeding blockade vs clinical change

patient_trials.quote: Tilavonemab was generally well tolerated but did not demonstrate efficacy in treating patients with early Alzheimer's disease.

efficacy.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
efficacy.note: Gosuranemab removed seeding-competent tau from AD brain homogenate and blocked AD-tau seeding in mouse primary neurons; TANGO had not read out.
efficacy.short: Product neutralizes AD seeds ex vivo
efficacy.quote: Preincubation of seed-competent AD-tau with gosuranemab significantly inhibited tau aggregation in mouse primary cortical neurons.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from Courade's ad-tau-seeding-assay under the run's identity rule: a different procedure (immunodepletion of homogenate, primary-neuron seeding, the humanized product rather than a mouse-IgG1 V-region graft) that made the opposite prediction for the same antibody (active here; 'essentially inactive' as antibody A there). If a checker treats the two AD-seed systems as one, these entries fold into that track as its own-data conflict.

efficacy.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
efficacy.note: Shulman names the AD-lysate and ISF depletion data as TANGO's preclinical basis; no dose changed CDR-SB at week 78.
efficacy.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC10724064); the model side is read at abstract level.
efficacy.reason: Seed removal ex vivo; CDR-SB unmoved
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison: Shulman 2023 writes 'This study is supported by preclinical data demonstrating the high binding affinity of gosuranemab to monomeric and aggregated forms of tau and its ability to remove seeding-competent forms of tau from AD brain lysate' (citing Sopko 2020 as ref 18) and then reports no CDR-SB effect at any dose; the authors' explanation is that 'targeting an N-terminal tau epitope may not sufficiently capture extracellular tau species responsible for mediating tau pathology propagation'. TANGO's registry primary is safety with CDR-SB the powered efficacy gate (poc_gate). Year is the paper's, the first time the model side was put beside the result; the registry posting (2022-11-08) carries no model side.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of seed removal vs clinical change

patient_trials.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control

efficacy.model: QSP model of synaptic-cleft tau secretion, antibody capture and uptake, coupled to PBPK
efficacy.note: ODE model of secretion, antibody capture and uptake in the synaptic cleft with PBPK-derived CSF/ISF exposure, built to simulate the gosuranemab, tilavonemab and semorinemab trials.
efficacy.short: QSP cleft model built after failures
efficacy.quote: Integration with a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model allowed us to simulate clinical trials of anti-tau antibodies gosuranemab, tilavonemab, semorinemab, and anti-aSyn antibodies cinpanemab and prasineuzumab.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the model was built after the Tauriel (2022) and the gosuranemab and tilavonemab PSP (2021) failures were public. Separate in-silico track: a different system from the mice and the seeding assays, built to explain rather than to select.

efficacy.model: QSP model of synaptic-cleft tau secretion, antibody capture and uptake, coupled to PBPK
efficacy.note: Simulated 45-99% CSF engagement but 1-3% in the cleft, cutting oligomeric-tau uptake by under 1% even at 8100 mg; reproduces semorinemab's Tauriel miss.
efficacy.quote: On the other hand, due to the avid binding of oligomeric tau to postsynaptic receptors, gosuranemab maximally reduces the uptake of oligomeric tau by 0.008%.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. For the AD context the member patient datum the paper simulates is semorinemab's Tauriel (Teng 2022); gosuranemab and tilavonemab are simulated against their PSP trials, and the paper notes gosuranemab's AD data were unreported when it was written. Senior author Courade is the UCB antibody-D author (Courade 2018).
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): parameterized from the members' phase 1 PK and run after the phase 2 outcomes were known, so it reproduces rather than predicts: 'retro', never 'same'. The comparison is stated in the paper ('Both tilavonemab in progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and semorinemab in AD failed to change clinical progression', with the simulations beside them). Its CSF-engagement figures are fitted to the observed CSF data, so no engagement entry is scored.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction: simulated <1% reduction in oligomeric-tau uptake vs no clinical effect

patient_trials.quote: semorinemab did not slow clinical AD progression compared with placebo throughout the 73-week study period

efficacy.model: Spatial Monte Carlo (MCell) model of antibody and tau trajectories in the synaptic cleft
efficacy.note: Spatial Monte Carlo of the cleft: under 0.5% of ISF antibody enters and seed uptake falls under 10%, using the same three members' parameters.
efficacy.quote: These simulations using a detailed and realistic biological environment provide a possible explanation for the clinical trial failures of anti-tau and anti-αsynuclein antibodies.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC12256572). Antibody parameters are those of semorinemab, tilavonemab and gosuranemab; the paper names no trial endpoint, the failures are cited (Teng 2022, Hoglinger 2021, Dam 2021).
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction by the same group with a different numerical method and the same conclusion; kept on the QSP track as a strengthening entry because it makes the same prediction. Its own account of the 2023 model: 'This model was able to provide a rationale for the observed clinical trial failures of three different antibodies (gosuranemab, tilavonemab and semorinemab) tested at very high doses (up to 120 mg/kg).'
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction: simulated <10% reduction in seed uptake vs no clinical effect

patient_trials.quote: semorinemab did not slow clinical AD progression compared with placebo throughout the 73-week study period

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkeys and tau-transgenic mice (PK/PD; toxicology species unpublished)
safety.note: Mice and monkeys were dosed for PK and engagement; no toxicology prediction was published to compare with the clean phase 1-2 safety.
safety.short: Clean in patients; no model comparison
safety.quote: No concerning safety signals were observed in the phase 1 clinical trial at single doses up to 16,800 mg and multiple doses totaling 33,600 mg in a month.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); toxicology species and findings are not public and no FDA review exists (no BLA filed for any member; manifest rows 4405, 5300, 5679, 7971 are 'no NDA/BLA').
safety.judgement: Kept as untested rather than an empty cell because the species were dosed for this class. All four phase 2 trials reported acceptable safety (Teng 2022, Florian 2023, Shulman 2023, Monteiro 2023, Fleisher 2024); zagotenemab's higher AE incidence (85.1% vs 74.6%) 'was not attributable to any specific AE or category of AEs' (Fleisher 2024), so there is no harm a species was silent on. Separate track from the efficacy mice: a different system with a different (PK/tolerability) prediction.
